To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tyrosylsulphotransferase is a key enzyme in the biosynthesis of the sulphate group in tyrosine of the peptide hormones.

the sulfation of tyrosl residues of secretory proteins is carried out by one or more enzymes which are identical or very similar in different tissues and that the sulfation is catalyzed by a tyrosylsufotransferase which is a microsomal enzyme.

(1) tyrosyl‐protein sulfation is catalysed by a single enzyme, (2) the sulfotransferase is a microsomal membrane‐bound enzyme, (3) the enzyme has a broad specificity for its protein substrates, and (4) the enzyme has an absolute requirement for a tyrosine residue adjacent to a basic residue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sulfation of tyrosl residues in secretory proteins from different tissues.
the sulfation of proteins and glycosaminoglycans by sulfotransferases.
the study of sulfotransferases in rat cerebral tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tyrosylsulphotransferases are not identical, but are closely similar.
the tyrosylsufotransferase activity of rat brain is identical to the tyrosyltransferase of the liver.
the tyrosylsulfo transferase activity of the brain is similar to the tyrosyl sulfo transferase activity in the intestine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tyrosylsulphotransferase activities are present in the brain, liver, kidney and adrenal glands, and in the microsomes of these organs.

the sulfotransferase activity of rat brain microsomes, which is responsible for the sulfation of tyramine and tyrosine residues in secretory proteins, is not specific for tyrosine residues but is also able to sulfonate tyrosine residues located in a peptide chain.
the sulfotransferase activity of the brain is not specific for cholecystokinn, but that the enzyme is capable of sulfating a variety of tyrosine‐containing peptides.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the sulfation of tyrosl residues in proteins can be performed in the endoplasmic reticulum by a sulfotransferase which is identical or closely similar to the one responsible for the sulfation of cholecystokiniin in the intestine.
the tyrosylsulphotransferases responsible for the sulphation of tyrosyl residues of secretory proteins in the brain and the liver are identical or closely related.
